analysis: Natural Killer T (NKT) cells are a unique subset of T lymphocytes that recognize lipid antigens presented by CD1d molecules. This is a well-established characteristic of NKT cells, distinguishing them from other T cell subsets. They do not primarily have KIR-type antigenic receptors, which are more characteristic of natural killer (NK) cells. While NKT cells do have T cell receptors (TCRs), the defining feature relevant to this question is their recognition of lipids bound to CD1 molecules. Although NKT cells can produce various cytokines, including IL-17, the outstanding feature of NKT cells is their recognition of lipid antigens presented by CD1 molecules.
